marketPulse: Reversal: Iran Strikes Qeshm Port, Ceasefire Breach Declared. Semis Finally Buckle. Russell -1.74%. Datadog +29% Lone Bright Spot.
marketPulseSubtext: S&P 500 -0.38% to 7,337.11, Nasdaq -0.13% to 25,806.20, Dow -0.63% to 49,596.97, Russell 2000 -1.74% to 2,836.80 — snapping all-time high streaks. Every major sector declined, led by Energy -1.95% and Industrials -1.66%. Late-session catalyst: US military struck Iran's Qeshm Port and Bandar Abbas — Iran declared a ceasefire violation. Oil reversed from session lows, Brent closed at $100.06, WTI $94.81. Datadog +29% was the session's standout on a 43% EPS beat. Rackspace +63% on AMD partnership. ARM -6% on chip supply concerns. Broadcom -4% on $18B chip deal financing complexity. US Trade Court ruled Trump's 10% global tariff unconstitutional. Jobless claims 200K (below 206K estimate). AH: Airbnb +8%, Expedia +7%, Block +5%. Iran Qeshm situation still developing.
topDriver: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Port late session — Iran declares ceasefire breach, oil spikes, all indices reverse from morning highs. Market paid the price for pricing in a peace deal that isn't signed.
narrativeSummary: May 7 was the session where the market discovered it had priced in a peace deal that doesn't exist yet. The day started with genuine momentum — futures were up, Iran was reviewing a 14-point US proposal, jobless claims came in below estimates at 200K, and Datadog exploded 29% on a 43% EPS beat. The morning looked like a consolidation after five record sessions. Then the afternoon arrived. US military struck Iran's Qeshm Port and Bandar Abbas — Fox News confirmed via a senior US official who said the strikes 'do not mean a restarting of the war.' Iran's armed forces spokesperson immediately declared a ceasefire violation, saying US forces hit civilian areas 'with cooperation of some regional countries.' Iran responded with attacks on US military vessels east of the Strait and south of Chabahar port. Commercial vessel traffic through Hormuz dropped to one of its lowest points ever in the past 48 hours. The impact was immediate: oil reversed from session lows (WTI had been near $93), Brent closed at $100.06, every sector turned red. The Russell 2000 led the decline at -1.74% as industrials, energy, and healthcare — its primary exposures — all sold off. The Dow fell 313 points on CAT -3.37% and JPMorgan -2.74%. Semiconductors buckled for the first time in weeks — ARM -6% on chip supply concerns (Arm's own Q1 FY27 guide implied a slowdown), Broadcom -4% on a report that its $18B chip deal requires Microsoft to buy 40% of output. Apple touched an all-time intraday high of $290.33 but could not hold gains. A US Trade Court ruling striking down Trump's 10% global tariff added an unexpected legal complication — though it will face appeal. The post-close picture was more complicated: Airbnb, Expedia, and Block all reported strong AH beats, and the diplomatic track remains open with Iran still 'reviewing messages' via Pakistani mediators.
macroStressSubtext: Iran strikes Qeshm Port, declares ceasefire breach — MSI snaps back from Elevated to High. Situation fluid post-close.
rateCurveRead: Yields fell sharply across the curve on May 7 as the morning session priced in an Iran deal — the 10Y dropped to 4.36% (-7bps from May 6's 4.43%) and the 30Y retreated to 4.94% as oil's decline removed energy inflation premium from the long end. The 2Y fell 6bps to 3.87%, the most aggressive since the April ceasefire, as markets priced a more dovish Warsh on lower inflation. However the late-day Qeshm Port strike will partially reverse this overnight — expect the 10Y to open higher on Friday. The 2/10 spread compressed to +49bps from +50bps. Jobless claims 200K (below 206K estimate) and productivity +0.8% (below 1.1% estimate) were both supportive of a soft-landing narrative — before the evening's events. Source: Federal Reserve H.15, May 7, 2026 official release.

flowsRead: May 7 flows are dominated by two countervailing forces: the morning's Iran-deal optimism (bonds up, oil down, semis digesting) and the afternoon's Qeshm reversal (energy volatility, industrials selling, safety buying). The clearest signal is the semiconductor outflow — the first meaningful one in two weeks. ARM and Broadcom provided the specific catalysts, but the broader message is that the SOX trade needed a pause after a parabolic run. Datadog's $1.8B inflow confirms that enterprise cloud AI is now a separate trade from hardware AI — and it's working. Short-duration Treasuries at $2.1B inflow is the institutional read: no one is willing to be long duration overnight with Qeshm developing.

drivers.name: Iran Qeshm Port Strikes — Ceasefire Breach Declared, Hormuz Traffic at Lowest Point Ever
drivers.detail: US military struck Iran's Qeshm Port and Bandar Abbas late in the trading session. A senior US official told Fox News the strikes 'do not mean a restarting of the war or an end to the ceasefire.' Iran's armed forces spokesperson declared a ceasefire violation and said Iran responded with attacks on US military vessels east of the Strait of Hormuz and south of Chabahar port. CNN reported commercial vessel Hormuz traffic dropped to one of its lowest points ever in the past 48 hours. The diplomatic track remains open — Iran is still 'reviewing messages' via Pakistani mediators and has not finalized its response to the 14-point US proposal. The market had started the day pricing in a deal; the Qeshm strike reversed that trade rapidly in the final hour. hormuzclosurePct downgraded from 20% back to 8%.

drivers.name: Datadog +29% — Enterprise Cloud AI Monitoring the Cleanest AI Pick-and-Shovel
drivers.linked: DDOG, cloud AI, enterprise software, AICS
drivers.source: Datadog IR press release, Yahoo Finance, Bloomberg
drivers.detail: Datadog Q1 2026: revenue $1.006B (+32% YoY), EPS $0.60 vs $0.42 consensus (43% beat), operating cash flow $335M, FCF $289M. FY 2026 guide raised to $4.30-4.34B vs $4.09B expected — a 6%+ beat. Largest single-day gain in 6 years. CEO Olivier Pomel: '32% revenue growth, $335M operating cash flow.' Datadog's platform monitors and secures every component of the AI infrastructure stack — from GPU clusters to LLM APIs. As the AI hardware supercycle matures, observability becomes mandatory at scale. enterpriseSoftwareAIRevGrowth raised to 24.6% incorporating Datadog.

drivers.name: ARM and Broadcom Stumble — Supply Constraints and Deal Financing Complexity Introduce Execution Risk
drivers.detail: ARM fell 6% on two concerns: (1) Q1 FY27 revenue guide of $1.26B ($1.21-1.31B range) implies sequential deceleration from Q4's $1.49B as the licensing lumpy model means revenue won't be linear; (2) chip supply constraints for the new AGI CPU — ARM's first silicon in 35 years needs foundry capacity that is globally constrained. Broadcom fell 4% after The Information reported the $18B first phase of its OpenAI chip venture requires Microsoft to purchase approximately 40% of chips to make financing viable. If MSFT declines, Broadcom must finance the phase alone — a meaningful balance sheet commitment. Both stories introduce execution risk into what had been viewed as clean AI infrastructure plays.

drivers.name: US Trade Court Strikes Down 10% Global Tariff as Unconstitutional
drivers.linked: Trade policy, import costs, S&P consumer sectors
drivers.detail: A US Trade Court ruled against President Trump's 10% global tariff. The court found the tariff exceeded executive authority — the same legal argument that struck down the earlier Liberation Day tariffs at the Supreme Court. The administration will appeal immediately and the tariff likely remains in effect pending appeal, but the ruling introduces legal uncertainty. If upheld on full appeal, it would represent the most significant rollback of Trump's trade policy and could lower consumer goods prices materially — a positive for core PCE. Market reaction was muted as most assumed the tariff stays pending appeal.

drivers.name: Labour Market Resilience — Jobless Claims 200K (Below 206K) Amid Iran Chaos
drivers.detail: Initial jobless claims 200K for week ended May 2 — 6K below the 206K consensus, up 10K from prior week's revised level. Continuing claims fell 10K to 1.77M. Labour market remains historically tight. Productivity +0.8% (below 1.1% estimate) suggests growth softening. Unit labour costs +2.3% (above 1.6% estimate) — wages running hot relative to productivity, meaning wage inflation is structural. Warsh's June 17 debut will face a still-tight labour market regardless of where Iran goes.

risks.title: Iran ceasefire formally ends — Qeshm strikes are developing post-close, Friday open uncertain
risks.desc: The most critical immediate risk. Iran's armed forces declared a ceasefire breach and responded with attacks on US vessels. If Iran's supreme leader formally ends the ceasefire Friday morning, Brent will open near $110-115. The US official insists the strikes were targeted and 'do not mean a restarting of the war' — but Iran's reading is different. The next 12-24 hours are the most geopolitically sensitive since May 4's Monday selloff.

risks.title: Broadcom-OpenAI chip deal contingent on Microsoft — $18B first phase at risk if MSFT declines
risks.desc: The Information's report that Broadcom's $18B chip deal requires Microsoft to purchase ~40% of output introduces a key dependency: if MSFT declines (prioritising its $190B capex programme over new chip commitments), Broadcom must finance the phase alone or restructure the deal. This is a large-scale version of the same capex-without-visible-demand concern that punished Meta. The deal was announced as a major AI infrastructure milestone — contingency disclosure changes the risk profile.

risks.title: ARM sequential guide-down — manufacturing pivot risk as first chip in 35 years faces supply ramp
risks.desc: ARM's Q1 FY27 guide ($1.26B) implies a sequential step-down from Q4's $1.49B. The licensing model is inherently lumpy, so this may be a timing issue — but it also reflects the reality that the AGI CPU chip manufacturing programme is early-stage. Morgan Stanley's Equal-Weight downgrade (despite raising PT to $150) had flagged this risk: 'near-term risks as Arm transitions into chip manufacturing.' At 100x+ forward earnings, any guidance miss is deeply punished.

risks.title: Russell 2000 -1.74% — small-cap breadth reversing sharply on Iran re-escalation
risks.desc: The Russell's -1.74% was the worst single-day decline among major indices, erasing most of the all-time high gain from yesterday. Small caps are more exposed to Iran through: (1) energy cost pass-through (thinner margins), (2) industrial supply chain disruption, (3) healthcare cost inflation. The breadth expansion story of the past week just took a one-day reversal — if Qeshm develops further Friday, the Russell could extend its decline significantly.

risks.title: Gas prices $4.56/gallon national average — political pressure building on Trump from both parties
risks.desc: National average gas prices hit $4.56/gallon on Thursday — up from $2.98/gallon before the Iran war. NPR/PBS/Marist poll: 81% of Americans feel major or minor household budget strain from fuel prices. 63% blame Trump (including 32% of Republicans). Political cost of the Iran war is now showing up in polls and could pressure the administration toward a faster deal or domestic energy response. California at $6.01/gallon. Social pressure is an accelerant for diplomacy.

strategies.title: Long enterprise cloud AI software — DDOG, SaaS picks decoupled from Iran noise
strategies.body: Datadog's 43% EPS beat and 6% FY guide raise confirm enterprise cloud AI monitoring is a structural growth trade independent of Iran, hardware supply constraints, or semi valuations. The pick-and-shovel analogy is exact: as AI models proliferate, observability, security, and monitoring become mandatory at every enterprise. enterpriseSoftwareAIRevGrowth now 24.6%, the best reading in the cycle. Rackspace +63% on AMD partnership extends the sovereign and regulated cloud angle.
strategies.trigger: Enterprise AI monitoring revenue growth >20% for 2 consecutive quarters

strategies.title: Iran binary position — long Brent puts (deal) AND long XLE calls (escalation)
strategies.body: The Qeshm strike creates a clean binary: either Iran formally ends the ceasefire (Brent $110-120, XLE spikes) or the back-channel absorbs it and the deal proceeds (Brent $85-90, XLE collapses). Both tails are large. A strangle on energy captures either outcome. The cost of the strangle is the premium — at current implied vol, the oil-price range is wide enough that both legs are in-the-money at their respective extremes.
strategies.trigger: Iran formal ceasefire declaration OR 14-point framework signed

strategies.title: Reduce ARM — supply ramp risk and sequential guide-down at 100x forward earnings
strategies.body: ARM's -6% day on the Q1 FY27 guide is a warning. The $1.26B Q1 FY27 midpoint is a 15% sequential decline from Q4's $1.49B. Even if that's licensing timing, it gives bears ammunition at 100x+ forward P/E. The manufacturing pivot to the AGI CPU is the right strategy long-term but introduces execution risk that wasn't priced in at $237. Morgan Stanley's Equal-Weight at $150 PT is not entirely wrong. Trim to a smaller position ahead of the supply ramp.
strategies.trigger: ARM Q1 FY27 guidance confirmed below $1.3B AND foundry capacity update at investor day

strategies.title: Long TLT — if Iran deal closes, 10Y could fall to 3.9-4.0% rapidly
strategies.body: With the 10Y at 4.36% and WTI near $95, the math for a rapid rate rally is compelling if Iran formally signs: WTI falls to $80-85, PCE trend falls toward 2.8-2.9%, Warsh's June 17 inaugural statement shifts from hawkish to neutral, and the fiscal risk premium partially compresses. TLT at 4.36% 10Y offers 6-8% total return to 3.8-4.0%. The risk is obvious — Qeshm could spike oil and rates overnight.
strategies.trigger: Formal Iran peace agreement signed AND WTI sustained below $90
